Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$ on the four-dimensional affine Minkowski space $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, as in the selected HEFT spacetime convention. Use the trivial spin structure, spinor bundle $S=M\times\mathbb C^4$, gamma matrices satisfying $\{\gamma^\mu,\gamma^\nu\}=2\eta^{\mu\nu}I$, chirality operator $\gamma_5=-i\gamma^0\gamma^1\gamma^2\gamma^3=i\gamma_0\gamma_1\gamma_2\gamma_3$, and eigensubbundles $S_\pm=\ker(\gamma_5\mp I)$. Here $\gamma_0=-\gamma^0$, $\gamma_j=\gamma^j$ for spatial $j$, and $\bar\psi=\psi^\dagger i\gamma^0$; choose $(i\gamma^0)^\dagger=i\gamma^0$ and $(\gamma^j)^\dagger=\gamma^j$. This matches the shared anomaly-matching data and Bilal's mostly-plus positive-chirality convention in Eq. (2.20), which fixes the sign of his anomaly formula. Take the trivial bundle for the fixed global symmetry group $H=SU(3)\times U(1)_V$, set the $SU(3)$ background connection to zero, and keep only the nondynamical $U(1)_V$ connection $B\in\Omega_c^1(M,\mathbb R)$ with curvature $G=dB$. Here $U(1)_V=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}$ and its charge-$q$ representation is $\rho_q(z)=z^q$ on $\mathbb C$. The background $B$ is not integrated over as a quantum gauge redundancy.

Let $\psi_+\in C_c^\infty(M,S_+\otimes\mathbb C_{(\mathbf1,+1)})$ and $\psi_-\in C_c^\infty(M,S_-\otimes\mathbb C_{(\mathbf1,0)})$ be complex Weyl fields in the indicated $SU(3)\times U(1)_V$ representations. Use $D_q=d+iqB$ on charge-$q$ fields and the fixed Lorentz-scalar chiral Dirac pairing $\bar\psi_+\psi_-$. Let $\Phi=v e^{i\theta}$ be a nonvanishing order-parameter field in $(\mathbf1,+1)$ with fixed modulus $v>0$ and smooth real phase $\theta\in C_c^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$. A dimensionless nonzero Yukawa parameter $y$ gives the mass term $-y\Phi\bar\psi_+\psi_-+\mathrm{h.c.}$, where h.c. denotes Hermitian conjugation, and heavy mass $M_H=|y|v>0$. The fermion fields have mass dimension $3/2$, $v$ and $M_H$ have mass dimension one, $B_\mu$ has mass dimension one, $G_{\mu\nu}$ has mass dimension two, and $\theta$ is dimensionless.

For $\alpha\in C_c^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$, use $B\mapsto B+d\alpha$, $\psi_+\mapsto e^{-i\alpha}\psi_+$, $\psi_-\mapsto\psi_-$, and $\Phi\mapsto e^{-i\alpha}\Phi$, hence $\theta\mapsto\theta-\alpha$. These transformations leave the Yukawa term invariant. In the anti-Hermitian product-group convention, the selected singlet has connection $iB$ and covariant derivative $d+iB$; in Bilal's Hermitian convention write $\mathscr A=-B$ and $\epsilon=-\alpha$, so $d-i\mathscr A=d+iB$ and the transformations agree. Let $\Gamma_H[B,\theta]$ denote the formal one-loop effective-action contribution of this Yukawa-massive pair, whose fermion mass is $M_H=|y|v>0$. For determining its local consistent-anomaly coefficient, separately use the Pauli–Villars-regulated one-loop triangle with one gauge-current insertion and two $U(1)_V$ background-connection insertions for a massless positive-chirality Weyl field in $(\mathbf1,+1)$. In this triangle calculation only, the physical loop has $M_0=0$ and weight $\eta_0=1$, while the three regulator loops have weights $\eta_1=\eta_3=-1$ and $\eta_2=1$, a positive scale $M_{\mathrm{PV}}$, and masses $M_1=M_3=M_{\mathrm{PV}}$, $M_2=\sqrt2M_{\mathrm{PV}}$, with $M_{\mathrm{PV}}\to\infty$ after subtraction. The $M_0=0$ physical loop belongs only to this massless triangle calculation; it is not the physical loop of $\Gamma_H$, whose mass remains $M_H>0$. Let $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{tri},0}(\alpha,B)$ denote the local consistent-anomaly variation computed from this massless triangle. It fixes the massless chiral representation's coefficient and is not the variation of the massive pair or a definition of its full determinant. Define the consistent anomaly as an infinitesimal effective-action variation, rather than as a covariant-current divergence. Add no non-invariant local counterterm to $\Gamma_H$; gauge-invariant local counterterms may be added. For an undetermined real coefficient $c$, the candidate Wess–Zumino functional is $\Gamma_c[B,\theta]=c\int_M\theta G\wedge G$; the theorem on this page fixes $c$.

After a constant rephasing of the neutral field absorbs the phase of $y$, the phase-dependent mass term is $-M_H e^{i\theta}\bar\psi_+\psi_-+\mathrm{h.c.}$. The pointwise invertible change of variables $\psi'_+=e^{-i\theta}\psi_+$, $\bar\psi'_+=e^{i\theta}\bar\psi_+$, and $\psi'_- =\psi_-$ removes $\theta$ from this mass term and changes the charged kinetic connection to $B_\theta:=B+d\theta$. Both $\psi'_+$ and $B_\theta$ are invariant under the simultaneous background transformation.

Use the Minkowski effective-action convention $Z_H[B,\theta]=\exp(i\Gamma_H[B,\theta])$, as a formal perturbative generating-functional notation. Let $\Gamma_R^M[B]$ denote the massless charged species' effective action in the selected consistent representative, with $\delta_\alpha\Gamma_R^M=\mathcal A_{\mathrm{tri},0}(\alpha,B)$. For compactly supported real $\theta$, define the local finite difference along the connected Abelian orbit by
$$\Delta_M[B,\theta]:=\Gamma_R^M[B+d\theta]-\Gamma_R^M[B]=\int_0^1\mathcal A_{\mathrm{tri},0}(\theta,B+t\,d\theta)\,dt.$$
This is a local perturbative difference, not a chosen global determinant phase. Adopt the scope-limited source-backed change-of-variables premise that the regulated old measure equals $J_M[B,\theta]$ times the new measure, with $J_M=\exp(-i\Delta_M)$ in this Minkowski convention. Its contribution to the effective action is therefore $\Gamma_J=(1/i)\log J_M=-\Delta_M$, on the perturbative logarithm branch vanishing at $\theta=0$. The transformed massive determinant is a functional $\mathcal F_M[B_\theta,M_H]$ of the invariant connection and constant mass, so the adopted local threshold relation is
$$\Gamma_H[B,\theta]=\mathcal F_M[B_\theta,M_H]-\Delta_M[B,\theta],\qquad \delta_\alpha\mathcal F_M[B_\theta,M_H]=0.$$
This source input concerns the anomalous local variation and its independence of $M_H$, not a construction or local expansion of the entire determinant. To compare signs with Preskill's Euclidean convention, continue as $\Gamma_E=-i\Gamma_M$ with oriented differential forms continued as in Bilal §10.1, and put $\Delta_E=-i\Delta_M$. Preskill's Eqs. (6.34), (6.43)–(6.45) then read $J_E=\exp(\Delta_E)$ and $\Gamma_{J,E}=-\log J_E=-\Delta_E$. Neither $J_E$ nor $\log J_E$ is the Minkowski effective-action term. Since $B_\theta$ is invariant, $\delta_\alpha\Delta_M=-\mathcal A_{\mathrm{tri},0}(\alpha,B)$, whereas $\delta_\alpha\Gamma_J=+\mathcal A_{\mathrm{tri},0}(\alpha,B)$. These opposite signs distinguish the finite difference from its effective-action contribution. No global or large-transformation claim about the Jacobian is made.

For low-energy use, a specified $n$-point background-field vertex of $\Gamma_H$, with $n\geq1$, is the coefficient multilinear in $n$ components chosen from $B_\mu$ and $\theta$ in the formal expansion about $B=0$, $\theta=0$, after Fourier-transforming each argument and removing the overall momentum-conservation delta. Its incoming real covectors $p_j=(p_{j0},p_{j1},p_{j2},p_{j3})\in\mathbb R^{1,3}$ satisfy $\sum_{j=1}^n p_j=0$; no on-shell condition is imposed. For that specified vertex set $E=\max_{1\leq j\leq n,\,0\leq\mu\leq3}|p_{j\mu}|$. The threshold condition $E/M_H\ll1$ concerns the finite set of external legs of that vertex, not the Fourier support of $B,\theta\in C_c^\infty(M)$, and supplies no Lorentz-invariant norm or quantitative expansion-remainder bound. The exact local anomaly variation below is independent of $E$. All determinant and anomaly data here are formal perturbative inputs; no exact functional integral or continuum limit is claimed.

Fix a four-dimensional smooth spacetime region $U\subseteq\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with a stated orientation, spin structure, boundary conditions, and unit system. A selected model specifies a continuous global symmetry group $H$, its action on the fields and observables, the nondynamical background connections, the field and jet domains, a regulator and measure or formal perturbative generating functional, and the admissible local counterterms. A background connection is nondynamical model data: it transforms under local changes of background trivialization but is not integrated over.

Let $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{bg},U}^{g,p}$ be the finite-jet horizontal $p$-forms of ghost number $g$ generated by the nondynamical background connections and their BRST ghost jets, without matter-field jets, and restrict the model’s nilpotent BRST differential $s$ and horizontal exterior derivative $d_H$ to this background subalgebra. An infinitesimal local anomaly representative is a local horizontal four-form $a_4\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{bg},U}^{1,4}$ such that $sa_4+d_Hb_3=0$ for some $b_3\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{bg},U}^{2,3}$. The **local perturbative ’t Hooft anomaly** of the specified global symmetry is the class $[a_4]$ in the relative cohomology $H^{1,4}(s\mid d_H)$ of this background subalgebra, with the quotient taken using exactly the model’s admissible four-dimensional background counterterms and total-derivative boundary convention. Its class is zero exactly when an admissible local counterterm removes the infinitesimal background variation modulo a boundary term.

Any prescribed noninvariance of the classical action or selected couplings is an explicit-symmetry-breaking insertion and is separated before assigning this quantum anomaly class. It is not, by itself, a measure anomaly. A claim of anomaly matching therefore assumes the stated classical symmetry, or carries such breaking insertions separately.

This definition applies to a global symmetry whose background is nondynamical. If the same local class concerns a field integrated over as a gauge redundancy, it is a local gauge anomaly, not a ’t Hooft anomaly; an uncancelled gauge anomaly obstructs the proposed gauging unless a separately specified cancellation mechanism is included. The definition addresses only infinitesimal transformations and makes no claim about large or disconnected transformations, determinant-line holonomy, torsion phases, or a physical continuum limit.

Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$ and flat oriented Minkowski spacetime $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-,+,+,+)$ and its standard spin structure. Fix Dirac matrices by $\{\gamma^\mu,\gamma^\nu\}=2\eta^{\mu\nu}I$ and $\gamma_5=-i\gamma^0\gamma^1\gamma^2\gamma^3=i\gamma_0\gamma_1\gamma_2\gamma_3$; set $P_+=(I+\gamma_5)/2$ and $P_-=I-P_+$. Here $\gamma_0=-\gamma^0$ and $\gamma_j=\gamma^j$ for spatial $j$; this is Bilal's mostly-plus positive-chirality convention, Eq. (2.20), used by the adopted source-normalized determinant law below. Reversing this chirality convention would reverse the one-species anomaly sign. The global symmetry group is the fixed global form $H=SU(3)\times U(1)_V$, acting on a finite multiset $S$ of massless positive-chirality Weyl fields. Each field is a Grassmann-odd smooth compactly supported section of $\operatorname{im}(P_+)\otimes V_i$, where $V_i$ carries a specified finite-dimensional unitary representation $R_i$ of $H$. The chiral kinetic operator is $\mathcal D_{+,i}=P_-i\gamma^\mu D_{\mu,i}P_+$ from positive to negative chirality; its regulated determinant phase is a formal perturbative input. The matter field has mass dimension $3/2$; the background potentials have mass dimension one, their curvature two-forms dimension two, and all $U(1)_V$ charges and trace coefficients are dimensionless. The backgrounds are global one-forms on the trivial bundles over $M$, vary smoothly, and have compact support; the global symmetry is not integrated over as a dynamical gauge redundancy.

For each species, the background covariant derivative is $D_{\mu,i}=\partial_\mu+\rho_{i*}(A_\mu,iB_\mu)$ in its representation, where $A$ is an anti-Hermitian $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ connection, $B$ is a real $U(1)_V$ connection, and $\rho_{i*}:\mathfrak{su}(3)\oplus i\mathbb R\to\mathfrak u(V_i)$ is the derived Lie-algebra representation. Set $F_A=dA+A\wedge A$ and $f=dB$, and write $A_i:=\rho_{i*}(A,iB)$ and $F_i:=dA_i+A_i\wedge A_i$; thus $D_{\mu,i}=\partial_\mu+(A_i)_\mu$. For $E=(\mathbf3,+1)$, $A_E=A+iB I_3$ and $F_E=F_A+ifI_3$; for $E^*=(\bar{\mathbf3},-1)$, $A_{E^*}=-A^T-iB I_3$ and $F_{E^*}=-F_A^T-ifI_3$. Local transformations are $A\mapsto g^{-1}Ag+g^{-1}dg$ and $B\mapsto B+d\alpha$ for compactly supported $g: M\to SU(3)$ and $\alpha:M\to\mathbb R$; the $U(1)$ group element is $e^{i\alpha}$. Let $c$ be the ghost-number-one odd $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ ghost and $\eta$ the ghost-number-one odd real $U(1)_V$ ghost. The finite-jet BRST differential for $\mathfrak h=\mathfrak{su}(3)\oplus i\mathbb R$ is specified on components by $sA_\mu=\partial_\mu c+[A_\mu,c]$, $sc=-[c,c]/2$, $sB_\mu=\partial_\mu\eta$, $s\eta=0$, and $s\psi_i=-\rho_{i*}(c,i\eta)\psi_i$; it acts on jets by commuting with total derivatives. The $U(1)_V$ factor is central. On horizontal forms use the supplier's extension $s(dx^\mu\wedge a)=-dx^\mu\wedge s(a)$, so $sd_H+d_Hs=0$. In particular the whole one-form obeys $sB=-d_H\eta$; the positive component rule is not a whole-form equation.

For an ordinary compactly supported infinitesimal parameter $\epsilon=\epsilon^aT_a:M\to\mathfrak{su}(3)$ and $\alpha:M\to\mathbb R$, define a linear map $\mathcal E^p_{\epsilon,\alpha}$ from ghost-number-one background horizontal $p$-forms to ordinary $p$-forms. In the unique normal form with all $dx$ factors to the left and the single ghost jet to the right, replace $c_I^a$ by $\partial_I\epsilon^a$ and $\eta_I$ by $\partial_I\alpha$, leaving background jets unchanged. Every such form has precisely one ghost factor because the background algebra has no negative-ghost generators. This is a linear map on that homogeneous component, not an algebra homomorphism on the exterior ghost algebra. It commutes with $d_H$. If $C_p$ is ghost-free, the finite-jet chain rule gives $\mathcal E^p_{\epsilon,\alpha}(sC_p)=(-1)^p\delta_{\epsilon,\alpha}C_p$: the sign moves $s$ past the $p$ coordinate one-forms, and the component rules give the ordinary infinitesimal field variation. Thus in physical degree four $\mathcal E^4(sC_4)=\delta C_4$, and $d_H$-exact terms evaluate to ordinary total derivatives. The degree-five descent is first formed on the formal auxiliary extension used for the degree-six polynomial, before restriction to $M$; there $\mathcal E^5(sI_5)=-\delta I_5$. Consequently $sI_5+d_HI_4^{(1)}=0$ yields the physical convention $\delta I_5=d_H\mathcal E^4(I_4^{(1)})$.

The anomaly-matching data include one common Pauli–Villars subtraction prescription for the chiral triangle graphs, with opposite-statistics regulator fields and regulator masses taken to the large-mass limit, together with the consistent effective-action variation convention and compact-support boundary conditions. The local anomaly complex is the finite-jet background subalgebra generated by $A,B$ and their BRST ghosts, with no matter-field jets, so its ghost-number-zero four-forms are precisely the admitted local counterterms. We quotient by all such finite-jet local counterterms and by compactly supported total derivatives; no background-gauge-invariance condition is imposed on an individual counterterm. In particular, for real dimensionless $\lambda$, the four-form $C_4=\lambda B\wedge K_3(A)$ is admitted, where $K_3(A):=\operatorname{tr}(A\wedge dA+\tfrac23A\wedge A\wedge A)$. As an explicit source-backed one-loop input, after the regulator masses are taken to infinity this selected prescription assigns to each positive-chirality species $R_i$ the consistent local anomaly obtained by descent from $\mathcal I_6(R_i,A_i)$ of the preceding cubic-polynomial definition. The fixed linear descent map is normalized by $\mathcal I_6=dI^{(0)}_5$, $sI^{(0)}_5+d_HI^{(1)}_4=0$, and $sI^{(1)}_4+d_HI^{(2)}_3=0$, with $\delta_{\epsilon,\alpha}\Gamma=\sum_{i\in S}\int_M\mathcal E^4_{\epsilon,\alpha}(I^{(1)}_4(R_i,A_i))$. This determinant law is an adopted regulator input in the data, not a locally derived theorem about every regulator. The total polynomial is $\mathcal I_6^{\mathrm{tot}}=\sum_{i\in S}\mathcal I_6(R_i,A_i)$, and its local anomaly class is interpreted using the preceding local ’t Hooft-anomaly definition. No large-transformation test, torsion calculation, mixed gravitational term, dynamical gauge quantization, or continuum-existence result is included.

derivations.claim: From [F1], $G'=d(B+d\alpha)=G+d^2\alpha=G$, while $\delta_\alpha\theta=-\alpha$. Thus $G\wedge G$ is invariant under the specified small background transformations.

By [F3], the linear map $\mathcal E^4_{0,\alpha}$ sets the $SU(3)$ ghost jets to zero and replaces each $U(1)_V$ ghost jet $\eta_I$ by $\partial_I\alpha$; for every ghost-free background four-form $C_4$, $\mathcal E^4_{0,\alpha}(sC_4)=\delta_{0,\alpha}C_4$, so its degree-four sign is positive. The model's $\gamma_5=-i\gamma^0\gamma^1\gamma^2\gamma^3$ is Bilal's mostly-plus positive-chirality matrix; in particular $\gamma_0=-\gamma^0$, so this equals his $i\gamma_0\gamma_1\gamma_2\gamma_3$. In Bilal's Hermitian convention [A1], $\mathscr A=-B$ and $\epsilon=-\alpha$, so $d-i\mathscr A=d+iB$ and the transformations agree with [F1]. For the positive-chirality $SU(3)$ singlet of $U(1)_V$ charge one in [F3], $\operatorname{tr}_R(1)=1$ and $d(\mathscr A\wedge d\mathscr A)=d(B\wedge G)=G\wedge G$; the Abelian cubic term vanishes. Inserting these values into [A1] gives $-\frac{1}{24\pi^2}\int_M(-\alpha)G\wedge G=+\frac{1}{24\pi^2}\int_M\alpha G\wedge G=\mathcal A_{\mathrm{tri},0}(\alpha,B)$ for the massless chiral triangle. To evaluate the finite difference, integrate this infinitesimal identity along $B_t=B+t\,d\theta$. Since $dB_t=G$, it gives $\Delta_M=\int_0^1\mathcal A_{\mathrm{tri},0}(\theta,B_t)\,dt=\frac1{24\pi^2}\int_M\theta G\wedge G$. Under the simultaneous transformation $B+d\theta$ is invariant, so $\delta_\alpha\Delta_M=-\frac1{24\pi^2}\int_M\alpha G\wedge G=-\mathcal A_{\mathrm{tri},0}$. The adopted relation [F1], [A2] has invariant $\mathcal F_M[B_\theta,M_H]$ and effective-action term $-\Delta_M=(1/i)\log J_M$; its variation is therefore $+\mathcal A_{\mathrm{tri},0}$, independent of $M_H$. The neutral partner has zero $U(1)_V$ charge. Hence $\delta_\alpha\Gamma_H=+\frac{1}{24\pi^2}\int_M\alpha G\wedge G=\mathcal A_H(\alpha,B)$.

Vary the displayed local functional: $\delta_\alpha\Gamma_{\mathrm{WZ}}=-\frac{1}{24\pi^2}\int_M((\delta_\alpha\theta)G\wedge G+\theta\,\delta_\alpha(G\wedge G))=+\frac{1}{24\pi^2}\int_M\alpha G\wedge G=\mathcal A_H(\alpha,B)$ by step 1.1 and step 1.2.

Linearity of infinitesimal variation gives $\delta_\alpha(\Gamma_L+\Gamma_{\mathrm{WZ}})=\mathcal A_L+\mathcal A_H=\delta_\alpha(\Gamma_L+\Gamma_H)$ by step 1.2 and step 2.1. The equality is of the selected local representatives and therefore also determines their classes modulo the admissible counterterms in [F2]; it concerns only the connected, infinitesimal background transformations.

The coefficient in $\Gamma_{\mathrm{WZ}}$ is the fixed dimensionless number $-1/(24\pi^2)$ and contains no factor of $M_H^{-1}$; the low-energy interpretation of the specified vertex is restricted by $E/M_H\ll1$. Thus the anomaly-carrying term is unsuppressed in the heavy-mass coefficient, without any claim of convergence or a quantitative remainder bound.

Adopt the source-derived consistent-anomaly formula for a positive-chirality Weyl field in representation $R$, written in Bilal's Hermitian convention,

$$\delta_{\epsilon}\Gamma_R=-\frac{1}{24\pi^2}\int_M\operatorname{tr}_R\!\left(\epsilon\,d\left(\mathscr A\wedge d\mathscr A-\frac{i}{2}\mathscr A\wedge\mathscr A\wedge\mathscr A\right)\right).$$
